questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: The highest or lowest speed you are allowed to drive
The speed you should drive in heavy traffic
The speed you should drive in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest speed you are allowed to drive
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest or lowest safe speed allowed on a road. The highest limits are for perfect conditions. You must drive slower when conditions are not safe.

questions.question: Driving while distracted by any activity:

options.text: Usually makes the driver react slower to hazards.
Usually makes the driver go faster.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually makes the driver react slower to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions make drivers react slower to traffic and dangers on the road. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: A lower speed zone is starting.
A lower speed zone is ending.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lower speed zone is ending.
questions.explanation: Do not drive faster than the school zone speed limit during the times shown. The "End school zone" sign marks where the lower speed zone ends.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb:

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: To stop your car from rolling into traffic when parked uphill, turn your wheels sharply away from the curb. If there is no curb, turn your wheels sharply toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: When another car is tailgating you:

options.text: Move to the right lane if it is open.
If the right lane is not open, wait until the road ahead is clear and slowly reduce your speed to let the tailgater drive around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If a car is tailgating you and the right lane is open, move to the right. If the right lane is not open, wait until the road ahead is clear and slowly reduce your speed. This lets the tailgater pass you. Never brake suddenly because this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the bridge or overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not go forward if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (in this case, 13 feet 6 inches).

questions.question: You must drive carefully near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: He or she is a police officer.
He or she has balance problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: He or she is blind.
questions.explanation: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down, yield the right-of-way, and proceed with caution. Be ready to stop to prevent injury to the pedestrian.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped and yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to special situations or dangers ahead.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle stopped on the side of the road:

options.text: Move out of the lane next to the stopped vehicle or slow down.
Pull off the road behind the stopped vehicle.
Move to the lane next to the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move out of the lane next to the stopped vehicle or slow down.
questions.explanation: The Move Over Law protects police, emergency workers, tow truck drivers, sanitation workers, and utility workers on the side of the road. You must move out of the lane next to the stopped vehicle. If you cannot safely change lanes, you must slow down to 20 mph below the speed limit.

questions.question: You must yield for emergency vehicles:

options.text: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must yield the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using a siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: You may carefully drive through an intersection with a yellow light if:

options.text: An emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, you should continue through carefully.

questions.question: You may cross double solid yellow lines:
questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, or to make a legal U-turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians are walking along the road ahead.
Watch for construction workers on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: A pedestrian crossing is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a pedestrian crossing is nearby. Drive carefully and watch for people crossing.

questions.question: Which substances can affect your driving and may result in a DUII (driving under the influence) arrest?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. This includes all alcoholic drinks, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medicines.

questions.question: To prevent fatigue on a long drive, you should:

options.text: Stop to rest every two hours.
Switch feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours for a break on long trips. If you get drowsy, pull over safely and rest or sleep.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area you:

options.text: Cannot see without turning your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are on the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: Which of these directs drivers into the correct lanes for turning on some highways?

options.text: White lines on the road edge
White arrows painted in the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows painted in the lanes
questions.explanation: White arrows show which lanes to use for going straight or turning.

questions.question: Florida law requires you to use headlights:

options.text: To alert other drivers around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Between sunset and sunrise.
questions.explanation: Florida law requires headlights between sunset and sunrise. Be extra careful when driving at night.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see an emergency vehicle. You should:

options.text: Keep driving until you see it.
Pull to the curb and check if it is on your street.
Slow down but don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and check if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but don't know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull to the right and stop until you are sure it is not coming toward you.

questions.question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:

options.text: Honk to alert the bicyclist you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give as much space as possible.
Speed ahead to get in front of the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists plenty of space. They have less protection than car drivers. Passing too fast can knock them off course.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to let others know you are there.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from the car in front of you.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than the traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: A safe distance lets you react to problems without emergency stops. Emergency stops can cause drivers behind you to crash into your car.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down, give them the right-of-way, and be ready to stop. This keeps them safe.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road or driveway?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn drivers you are entering.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert other drivers.
Drive out fast to merge smoothly with traffic.
Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and traffic on the roadway go first.

questions.question: When crossing a railroad track with no signals or gates, you should:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You can pass slower drivers while crossing the track.
Make sure your car can completely cross the tracks without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your car can completely cross the tracks without stopping.
questions.explanation: Check that you have enough space to cross all the way across before you drive onto the tracks. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing.

questions.question: A driver convicted of three traffic accidents within three years must:

options.text: Take a DHSMV-approved driver improvement course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a DHSMV-approved driver improvement course.
questions.explanation: The Three Crashes in Three Years Law requires drivers to take an approved course, complete professional driving training, and pass a special driving test. You must finish within 90 days or your license will be canceled.

questions.question: On long trips, how can you avoid getting drowsy?

options.text: Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
Move your eyes side to side while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
questions.explanation: Take regular breaks on long trips. Rest and stretch, even if you do not feel tired yet.

questions.question: A red traffic light means you must:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means stop at the stop line, before any crosswalk, and before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down and let traffic in the intersection or roadway you are entering go first.

questions.question: Driving too slowly is:

options.text: Safe for drivers who are not confident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Against the law.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly is illegal in Florida. Do not drive so slowly that you block or slow down traffic. Drive with the flow of traffic within the speed limit.

questions.question: If a car with high beams is coming toward you, look toward ____ of the road.
questions.correctAnswerText: The right side
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road when an oncoming car has high beams on. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see the road ahead until the car passes.
